enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

Sarah and \_\_\_\_\_\_ went to the market together.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Subject pronouns (I, he, she, we, they) come before the verb; object pronouns (me, him, her, us, them) follow it.

### Solution

The blank is part of the subject of "went", so the subject pronoun "I" is needed. **Answer: b.**

enonce_markdown:
Fill in the blank with a possessive pronoun.

This bag belongs to me. It is \_\_\_\_\_\_.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A possessive adjective (my) is followed by a noun; a possessive pronoun (mine) stands alone.

### Solution

The blank stands alone, without a noun after it, so we need a possessive pronoun (mine), not the possessive adjective "my". The answer is "mine".

enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

The little boy dressed \_\_\_\_\_\_ without any help from his mother.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Reflexive pronouns (myself, himself, themselves...) refer back to the subject of the verb.

### Solution

The subject and the object are the same person, so a reflexive pronoun is needed: "himself". **Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

The girl \_\_\_\_\_\_ won the quiz competition is my cousin.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Who = person as subject; whom = person as object; which = thing; whose = possession.

### Solution

The blank is the subject of "won" and refers to a person, so the relative pronoun "who" is needed. "Whom" is an object form and "whose" shows possession. **Answer: d.**

enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

I have not seen \_\_\_\_\_\_ in the compound this morning.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

After a negative verb use any- words (anybody, anything), not no- words.

### Solution

"Not seen" is already negative, so a second negative word (nobody, no one) would create a double negative. We use "anybody". **Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown:
Choose the best answer.

The boy \_\_\_\_\_\_ bicycle was stolen reported the matter to the police.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Whose links a person to the thing that belongs to him or her, and is followed by a noun.

### Solution

The blank shows that the bicycle belongs to the boy, so the possessive relative pronoun "whose" is needed. **Answer: d.**
